sources.entry: RelayTV - Turns a Linux box connected to a television into a local playback endpoint. Send links from a phone, browse Jellyfin or Emby libraries, play IPTV channels, and drive playback from Home Assistant or HTTP (alternative to Chromecast). (Source Code, Clients) GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: RelayTV turns a Linux box connected to a TV into a local-first media hub that plays links, library items, and IPTV channels, controlled from a phone or desktop browser.
summary.what_it_does: RelayTV runs on a Linux device (such as a Raspberry Pi or mini PC) attached to a television and owns playback locally. Users paste media URLs in the web UI or share links and local files from Android to the TV, and can play now, queue, or resume from history. It browses Plex, Jellyfin, and Emby libraries, and connects to Seerr for requests. It supports M3U/IPTV live channels with favorites, My Channels, and rewind within the buffered stream window. Phones connect by scanning a QR code on the TV's idle screen or opening the web UI on the same network, and it can import YouTube playlists into the queue. Automation is available through a Home Assistant media_player entity and a local HTTP API.
use_cases: send a video link from phone to TV
browse Jellyfin or Emby library on the TV
play IPTV channels on a television
shared family queue for movie night
control a TV from Home Assistant
request movies through Seerr and play them
how_to_run: Scan the QR code on the TV's idle screen or open the Web UI on the same network
Open Settings to connect media services
notable: Playback runs on the Linux box, so the phone can leave the remote page while the TV keeps playing
Shared queue and QR-code remote so family can add picks from their phones
Home Assistant media_player entity per screen plus a local HTTP API
IPTV with rewind limited to the buffered window and return-to-live
No RelayTV account or cloud dependency for core playback
caveats: Designed for a trusted LAN; should be behind a VPN or authenticated reverse proxy rather than exposed publicly
Optional RELAYTV_API_TOKEN needed to protect control requests on shared networks
Targets 64-bit arm64 or amd64 Linux hosts connected to a TV; Android companion app is optional
Private YouTube playlists need configured YouTube cookies; finite playlists capped at 1,000 videos
